terra.problem: The passage does not establish that the guards Peter sat with were the same kind of men involved in Jesus’ arrest.

Saying the council found no testimony to use, but the final two came forward with something, implies it found usable testimony. The text says it did not find the false testimony it sought, then reports what the two said without stating that conclusion.
The disciples’ earlier flight does not establish that they are nowhere near the room now. Peter himself has followed to the courtyard.
Calling boasting a fair guess because of Jesus’ words about sitting at the right hand of Power treats His statement irreverently.
The high priest says they need no more witnesses, not that they do not need testimony. The passage also does not say how long the search took.
The council’s verdict that Jesus deserves to die is not the same outcome as putting Him to death, which is what the chief priests and Sanhedrin were seeking.
At the first denial, Peter says he does not know what the servant girl is talking about. The explanation turns that into pretending not to know Jesus, which is not what he says at this point.
Suggesting an invented denial would have sounded smooth makes light of the serious sin in this moment.
The servant girl makes a statement; the text does not say she asks Peter a question.

The passage does not say anyone pointed at Peter.
The passage does not say Peter’s denials got louder.
Calling an imagined way to deny Jesus a smooth move and ending with a line about chuckling makes light of the serious sin in this moment.
The explanation places the events at night, a detail outside the supplied passage, without a reference for it.
